mmdlib_companion:creative_power.info:
*Creative Power Source*

Tests automatic energy export, per-face side settings and transfer statistics. Its buffer refills every tick without fuel.

Place it beside a powered companion machine and enable the connecting output face. It supplies up to 1,000 FE per enabled face per tick, subject to the receiving machine's input rules.

Disable one face and confirm that receiver stops charging while other enabled faces continue. Check Statistics for the actual transferred energy.

mmdlib_companion:crusher.info:
*Crusher*

Tests Java recipe processing, item reservations, a custom progress dial and editable screen controls. Supply FE and insert cobblestone to make gravel, gravel to make sand, or a supported ore to make raw material. The Recipes button opens JEI when installed.

Click the progress dial or processor button to pause and release reserved items. Resume to reclaim them. Settings lets you rename the machine, set its energy reserve and pause its lane; a reserve above the current charge holds processing.

The separate 4,000 mB tank tests fluid-container interactions and accepts water or lava, one fluid at a time. Left-click its gauge with a filled container to fill it; right-click with an empty container to drain it. You can also use a bucket on the block. Crushing does not consume this fluid.
mmdlib_companion:transmuter.info:
*Iron-to-Gold Converter*

Tests consuming an input and placing its product in the same physical slot, including reservations and a one-item slot limit.

Supply 4,000 FE and insert one iron ingot. After 200 work ticks, one gold ingot replaces it in that slot. Remove the gold before starting another cycle.

Pause during processing to release the input, then resume. With insufficient power, progress should stall without consuming the ingot.
mmdlib_companion:dual_crusher.info:
*Dual Crusher*

Tests two Java recipe lanes competing for the same input stack, output space and energy buffer.

Supply FE and insert several cobblestone or gravel items. Both lanes can advance when enough unreserved input and output space remain. Each lane has its own progress display and pause button.

Try a single input item: only one lane may claim it, and it must produce only one result. Pause one lane to release its reservations while the other keeps working. A full output must prevent new work without consuming input.
mmdlib_companion:logistics.info:
*Logistics Workbench*

Tests automation modules, filters and independent side settings for seven resource groups: item input, item output, two input tanks, two output tanks and energy. Recipe processing is disabled.

Place a chest or tank beside it. Open the side configuration, select a resource group, enable the connecting face and install a suitable puller, pusher, pump or relay. Powered modules need FE; filters can restrict which items or fluids move.

Configure different groups and faces independently, then check that only the intended resources transfer. Try an allow-list or deny-list filter and compare accepted and rejected contents. The workbench does not move input contents to its outputs by itself.
screen.mmdlib_companion.filter.whitelist: Whitelist: allow matching entries (click for blacklist)
screen.mmdlib_companion.filter.blacklist: Blacklist: block matching entries (click for whitelist)
item.mmdlib_companion.recovery_capsule.h: Use on a companion machine to restore pending fluids and energy. Any remainder stays in the capsule.
screen.mmdlib_companion.multiblock.info:
*Multiblock Test Bench*

Tests automatic placement of a three-block structure, shared resource ports, structure validation and dismantling. Place the bench with room for its two attached parts and keep the block above the middle part clear.

The far end is the socket for items, fluids and energy; its ports access the controller's displayed stores. The middle belt is not a resource port. Try opening the screen through a part and transferring resources through the socket.

While the structure is valid, Active ticks increases and the energy store gains 1 FE per tick. Obstruct the required clearance and check the status: work must stop until the structure is valid again.

Breaking any member dismantles the structure. Stored items and remaining fluid or energy must be recovered rather than duplicated or silently lost.
mmdlib_companion:simple_crusher.info:
*Simple Crusher*

Tests a machine defined entirely in XML: generated inventory and progress controls, recipe admission, ore recipe generation, side settings and shared upgrades.

Supply FE and insert cobblestone or gravel. Each produces gravel or sand respectively in 100 work ticks for 2,000 FE. Supported ore tags also generate ore-to-ingot recipes; JEI shows the recipes available in this pack.

Unrelated items should be refused at the input. Fill both output slots to check that blocked work leaves resources intact. Try the pause button, gearbox upgrades for faster work and capacitor upgrades for a larger energy buffer.
mmdlib_companion:simple_lava_furnace.inf:
*Simple Lava Furnace*

Tests fluid-powered recipes, a mod-provided smelting recipe generator, and recipe filters on both item and fluid inputs. It uses lava instead of FE.

Fill the 8,000 mB fuel tank with lava and insert an item with a smelting recipe, such as raw iron. The recipe reserves its item, lava and output space, then produces the smelted result when the cycle completes.

Water and unrelated items should be refused. Pause to release reservations, or fill the output to check that a new cycle cannot consume resources. JEI shows the generated recipes and their lava amounts.
mmdlib_companion:admission_demo.info:
*Admission Demo*

Tests storage admission without a recipe processor. This machine only stores accepted contents; it does not burn, smelt or distill anything.

Try coal in Burnable fuel, raw iron in Smeltable items and logs in Logs only. Stone should be refused by all three. The fuel slot uses a processor rule, the smelting slot uses a separate Java rule, and the log slot uses an item tag.

The Water tag tank accepts water. Configured fuel tag uses the lava tag by default. Recipe fluid accepts lava when the companion lava-smelting recipes are available. Water should be refused by those last two tanks.

Try manual insertion, hoppers or pipes, and fluid containers. The same restrictions should apply. The developer check changes the supplied fuel tag at runtime and verifies that fluid already stored is preserved.
mmdlib_companion:porting_workshop.info:
*Porting Workshop*

Tests a custom processor using typed item/fluid transactions, six-way placement, placer ownership and comparator output from an existing redstone source. It needs no FE.

Insert cobblestone and water: each work step converts one cobblestone and 25 mB of water into one stone. Fill the stone output and confirm that blocked work consumes neither input nor water.

Normal placement faces toward you. Sneak while placing to choose the clicked face instead. Successful placement records the player's identity and team; loading the machine must not count as another placement.

Attach a comparator, directly or through a solid block. Its strength follows stone output fullness: empty is 0 and a full stack is 15. No emitting redstone face needs to be enabled.
mmdlib_companion:parallel_workshop.info:
*Parallel Workshop*

Tests two XML recipe lanes running alongside a custom water-powered charge pump. Each lane has separate input/output slots and a pause control, while all three processors share one energy store.

Add water, or supply FE externally. Insert cobblestone in the left input and gravel in the right input. Expect gravel on the left and sand on the right. Each recipe takes 100 work ticks and 2,000 FE; the pump converts 1 mB of water into 100 FE per successful step.

Pause one recipe lane and confirm the other lane and pump can continue. Try gearboxes to accelerate work and reload the world to check saved state.

Java start/finish callbacks also record cycle counts and the last lane in the charge pump's saved state; they do not require CraftTweaker.
mmdlib_companion:shared_workshop.info:
*Shared Workshop*

Tests two XML recipe lanes sharing the same physical input while keeping separate outputs. Both lanes use the left input; the visible right input is intentionally unused.

Add water to run the charge pump, or supply FE externally. Put one cobblestone in the left input: only one lane may reserve it and only one gravel should be produced. Add a larger stack to let both lanes work.

The left lane ticks first and can claim the last available item. Pause it to let the right lane claim shared input. Output space and reserved inputs must never be counted twice. This example also binds a second name to the same energy store.
mmdlib_companion:battery_workshop.info:
*Battery Workshop*

Tests energy supplied by a custom BatteryBank processor. The gauge, recipe lanes, charging pump, automation and saved energy must all use the same store. It starts with 200,000 FE capacity and supports capacitor upgrades.

Put a Creative Power Source above it, or add water for the charge pump. Feed cobblestone or gravel to either recipe lane and watch the shared energy gauge fall as recipes work.

For manual play, charge it from above; this fixture currently exposes an input-only energy group to sided automation. Horizontal connections must refuse transfers. The developer checks also exercise unsided extraction. Pausing the battery processor disables direct energy connections, including existing ones, without pausing the recipe lanes or water pump.

Reload the world and check that the stored charge is preserved. It must not reveal a second, separate recipe buffer.
mmdlib_companion:paid_workshop.info:
*Paid Workshop*

Tests per-processor operating energy on the Parallel Workshop's unchanged recipes. Supply FE first, or seed at least 3 FE before relying on the water pump: the pump cannot start from an empty buffer.

Add water and cobblestone or gravel to the lane inputs. Each 100-step recipe still costs 2,000 FE, plus 5 FE per successful left-lane step or 9 FE per right-lane step: 2,500 FE left and 2,900 FE right per completed cycle.

The pump pays 3 FE before producing 100 FE from 1 mB of water, for a net gain of 97 FE. Pause the pump when comparing recipe costs in the gauge or Statistics.

Gearbox-accelerated steps each pay their cost. Idle, paused, held, stalled or blocked work must not charge operating energy. If a combined recipe and operating charge cannot be paid, energy and progress stay unchanged.
mmdlib_companion:facing_all.info:
*Facing Demo: All Directions*

Tests allowed facing directions and placement preference. Allows all six directions and faces toward the placer.

Place it while looking horizontally, up and down. The dispenser face should point back toward you.

The dispenser texture marks the front and gold marks the local top. For an upward or downward front, the gold top points north. Use the storage slot and side settings to check that resource faces follow the orientation. This is a storage-only example with no recipes or power requirement.
mmdlib_companion:facing_away.info:
*Facing Demo: Away from Player*

Tests allowed facing directions and placement preference. Allows all six directions and faces away from the placer.

Place it while looking horizontally, up and down. The dispenser face should point along your look direction, opposite to the All Directions demo.

The dispenser texture marks the front and gold marks the local top. For an upward or downward front, the gold top points north. Use the storage slot and side settings to check that resource faces follow the orientation. This is a storage-only example with no recipes or power requirement.
mmdlib_companion:facing_up.info:
*Facing Demo: Up Only*

Tests allowed facing directions and placement preference. Allows only an upward-facing front.

Place it from different sides and viewing angles. The dispenser face must always point up, regardless of where you stand.

The dispenser texture marks the front and gold marks the local top. For an upward or downward front, the gold top points north. Use the storage slot and side settings to check that resource faces follow the orientation. This is a storage-only example with no recipes or power requirement.
mmdlib_companion:facing_down.info:
*Facing Demo: Down Only*

Tests allowed facing directions and placement preference. Allows only a downward-facing front.

Place it from different sides and viewing angles. The dispenser face must always point down, regardless of where you stand.

The dispenser texture marks the front and gold marks the local top. For an upward or downward front, the gold top points north. Use the storage slot and side settings to check that resource faces follow the orientation. This is a storage-only example with no recipes or power requirement.
mmdlib_companion:facing_vertical.info:
*Facing Demo: Up or Down*

Tests allowed facing directions and placement preference. Allows only upward and downward fronts, preferring the direction toward the placer.

Look down while placing to get an upward-facing front, or look up to get a downward-facing front. Horizontal fronts must never be selected.

The dispenser texture marks the front and gold marks the local top. For an upward or downward front, the gold top points north. Use the storage slot and side settings to check that resource faces follow the orientation. This is a storage-only example with no recipes or power requirement.
mmdlib_companion:facing_asymmetric.info:
*Facing Demo: North, East or Up*

Tests allowed facing directions and placement preference. Allows only north, east and up, preferring the allowed direction nearest to the placer.

Place it from several sides, including ones that would normally choose south, west or down. The front must always remain north, east or up.

The dispenser texture marks the front and gold marks the local top. For an upward or downward front, the gold top points north. Use the storage slot and side settings to check that resource faces follow the orientation. This is a storage-only example with no recipes or power requirement.
